# The NVIC: priorities, preemption, latency: the exercise

<!-- Generated by tools/maintainer/build_exercise_readmes.py from the lesson page. Edit the lesson, then run the script. -->

Lesson: [The NVIC: priorities, preemption, latency](https://jouhis.github.io/embedded-course/lessons/0072-the-nvic.html). Read it first: the steps below refer to its diagrams and worked examples.

## Try it in Wokwi

The button on PB0 raises EXTI0. PB0 is routed to EXTI line 0 through the AFIO external-interrupt register (`AFIO->EXTICR[0]`, which the solution sets to the PB value, `AFIO_EXTICR1_EXTI0_PB`). The pin itself is on the default mapping in the [STM32F103x8/xB datasheet, "Pinouts and pin description" table](https://www.st.com/resource/en/datasheet/stm32f103c8.pdf). The EXTI0 handler is slow: it busy-waits for about 30 ms, at priority 2. A timer on TIM2 raises an update interrupt every 10 ms, at priority 0. The log records every event with a sequence number, so the order is visible on the serial monitor.

1. Open `projects/0072-the-nvic/starter` in VS Code, build with <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>B</kbd>, then start the simulator with <kbd>F1</kbd> → *Wokwi: Start Simulator*.
2. Your task: in `nvic_start()`, set the grouping to 3, set TIM2 to priority 0 and EXTI0 to priority 2, using `NVIC_EncodePriority`. Then press the button.
3. You will know it works when the serial monitor shows `TIM2 nested in EXTI0` between the `EXTI0 enter` and `EXTI0 exit` lines. Before you fix the priorities, the starter shows only `TIM2 tick` lines after the EXTI0 exit.

Look at the order in `tim2_tick_start()`: the update interrupt (`DIER.UIE`) is enabled only after the `EGR` write and the flag clear. The `UG` write sets the update flag, so with the interrupt already on it would raise a tick that never happened. In Wokwi it is worse: an interrupt raised by a store returns to that store and runs it again, so the program would hang before its first line. Also, Wokwi reads both priorities back as 0 in the startup line, even though the nesting shows they are set.

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint</summary>

Call `NVIC_SetPriorityGrouping(3)` first. Then pass the grouping to `NVIC_EncodePriority(3, preempt, 0)`. A lower preempt value wins.

</details>
